data.long_meaning: The name Kareef is derived from the Arabic word 'karf', which means 'noble' or 'generous'. In Islamic history, the name was given to individuals who demonstrated these qualities, such as kindness and generosity towards others. The name Kareef carries the meaning “Noble, generous, kind” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Kareef usually hope their child will grow to embody noble, generous, kind and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: The mystic and poet Sheikh Abdul-Qadir Jilani (1077-1166 CE) is also known as Shaikh-e-Kareem or the 'sublime Shaikh'. He was a prominent figure in the early Sufi movement in Iraq and is considered one of the founders of the Qadriyya Sufi order. The name 'Kareem' was given to him in recognition of his spiritual excellence and generosity towards his disciples.
historical_references.context: Early Sufi movement in Iraq, founder of the Qadriyya Sufi order

historical_references.reference: The Prophet Muhammad's (570-632 CE) cousin and companion, Ali ibn Abi Talib (600-661 CE), was also known by the epithet 'Amir al-Muminin' or 'Commander of the Faithful'. Another honorific title given to him during his caliphate was 'Abu Al-Hasan Al-Hussain Al-Kareem', which translates to 'Father of Hasan and Husain, the Noble'. This title highlights Ali's position as the father of the two esteemed grandsons of the Prophet Muhammad, Hasan and Husain, and emphasizes his noble character.
historical_references.context: Caliph of the Islamic Ummah (community), father of Prophet Muhammad's grandsons Hasan and Husain
